correctness.rationale: The rational linear transformation is a binomial identity. All 48 geometric lines lie on the resulting smooth signed diagonal quartic, and their exact pairwise intersection matrix has rational rank 20, saturating the K3 Picard bound. The Galois action on line coefficients is explicit, giving four exact idempotent-projector ranks 9,7,2,2. A self-contained Fraction-based checker and an independently written exact determinant incidence checker pass on the package files. Galois descent affects ranks only by torsion Brauer obstructions. No infinite claim is inferred from finite sampling: the 48-line enumeration is exhaustive for the Picard space because of the rank-20 bound.

The BHK paper calculates complex automorphism-invariant sublattices, not arithmetic Galois invariants; its listed symmetry ranks are not identified with this Galois action.

value.rationale: The rational Néron–Severi Galois module is a canonical arithmetic invariant of a K3 surface central to the new mirror-symmetry example. Determining all 20 dimensions and the characters simultaneously reveals a sharp 9 versus 16 versus 11 descent asymmetry that 8 rational lines or the geometric Picard rank 20 alone do not explain. It gives the precise splitting field of algebraic divisor directions, a natural complete classification useful when distinguishing arithmetic models and polarizations, without claiming a new mirror equivalence or an arbitrary slice.
